title: Reuse of a Completed Claimant Identity Verification on a Later Claim
content:
Under Claimant Identity Verification, a completed verification covers the claimant across claims for a limited time. A later claim of the same claimant may therefore rely on an earlier verification instead of opening a new case.

## The rule

A later claim of the same claimant does not open a new case when the claimant's latest verified date falls within the reuse period of the pathway that produced it, counted in calendar months from the verified date to the later claim's filed date, with month-end dates falling back to the last day of a shorter month.

The reuse does not apply, and a new case is opened, when the bank account or the mailing address on the claimant's profile changed within the re-verification window before the later claim was filed, or when any of the claimant's cases is fraud confirmed.

Reuse is decided per claim at filing and never reopens or extends the earlier case.

## Terms used

- **Latest verified date.** The latest verification completion date among all of the claimant's cases that reached verified, whether or not those cases have since closed.
- **Reuse period.** The number of calendar months set for the pathway on which that latest verification was completed.
- **Re-verification window.** The number of calendar days, before the later claim's filed date, within which a change of bank account or mailing address on the profile takes away the reuse.

## How the elements combine

| Latest verified date within the reuse period | Bank account or mailing address changed within the re-verification window before filing | Any of the claimant's cases fraud confirmed | Result for the later claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | no | no | reused; no new case is opened |
| yes | yes | either | reuse does not apply; a new case is opened |
| yes | either | yes | reuse does not apply; a new case is opened |

## Counting months, worked (hypothetical dates and periods)

- A verification completed on 31 August 2024 on a pathway with a hypothetical 18-month reuse period runs 18 calendar months to February 2026; February has no 31st day, so the end date falls back to 28 February 2026. A later claim filed on 10 February 2026 falls within the period; a later claim filed on 15 March 2026 does not.
- A verification completed on 15 May 2025 on a pathway with a hypothetical 12-month reuse period runs to 15 May 2026. A later claim filed on 2 April 2026 falls within the period.
- In the second case, if the claimant changed the mailing address on the profile 10 days before filing and the re-verification window is a hypothetical 30 days, the change falls inside the window: reuse does not apply and a new case is opened, even though the verification is still within its reuse period.

## Points of judgement

- Reuse is decided once for each claim, at its filing; it does not reopen the earlier case and does not extend its dates.
- The latest verified date counts even when the case that produced it has since been closed.
- A fraud confirmed case anywhere on the claimant's record takes away the reuse, whichever claim that case belongs to.
